boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Le Moyne study settings, from quiet library desks and reservable rooms to tutoring centers, lounge seating, and an outdoor terrace.

cards.entity_name: Noreen Reale Falcone Library — First Floor
cards.title: Bring the Group to the First Floor
cards.subtitle: Conversation-friendly library study space
cards.notes: Use the first floor when discussion is part of the assignment; conversation and group work are explicitly allowed in this library zone.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative library floor with study resources and nearby academic-support centers.
cards.evidence_claim: Le Moyne states that the library first floor permits conversation and group work and provides access to the Student Success Center and QRC.
cards.access_notes: Use during current Noreen Reale Falcone Library operating hours; conversation and group work are allowed on this floor.

cards.entity_name: Noreen Reale Falcone Library — Second Floor
cards.title: Take Quiet Work Upstairs
cards.subtitle: Designated quiet zone in Falcone Library
cards.notes: Head to the second floor for reading or concentrated solo work, and keep conversation elsewhere to respect its designated quiet-zone status.
cards.short_summary: The library’s documented quiet floor for focused individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Le Moyne identifies the library’s second floor as a designated quiet zone suitable for focused study.
cards.access_notes: Use during current library operating hours and observe the second floor’s designated quiet-zone expectations.

cards.title: Reserve a Room for Team Work
cards.subtitle: Self-service group-room reservations
cards.notes: Submit the self-service request at least two hours before your session, then bring the shared notes or presentation your group needs to finish.
cards.short_summary: Reservable library rooms intended for collaborative study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says Group Study Room reservations are self-service and must be submitted at least two hours before the room is needed.
cards.source_title: How do I reserve a room in the Library?
cards.access_notes: Reservation required through the library’s self-service system at least two hours in advance; availability is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Book a Room for Solo Focus
cards.subtitle: Self-service individual-room reservations
cards.notes: Reserve at least two hours ahead when you need an enclosed solo setting, and verify the room confirmation before planning your study block.
cards.short_summary: Individual library rooms available through advance self-service booking.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says Individual Study Room reservations are self-service and must be made at least two hours before the room is needed.
cards.source_title: How do I reserve a room in the Library?
cards.access_notes: Reservation required through the library’s self-service system at least two hours in advance; availability is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Work Through the Numbers at QRC
cards.subtitle: STEM study clinics and professional tutoring
cards.notes: Bring a specific calculus, statistics, computing, physics, or chemistry problem and use a clinic or tutor to work through the sticking point.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor library center for supported quantitative coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Le Moyne says the QRC is on the first floor of Falcone Library and provides study clinics and professional tutoring for quantitative subjects.
cards.access_notes: Located to the right after entering Falcone Library. Use posted QRC hours and check the current clinic schedule for course coverage.

cards.title: Pair Study Time With a Tutor
cards.subtitle: Individual and group academic support
cards.notes: Arrive with your course materials and a defined goal, then work with a mentor, tutor, or academic coach in an individual or group session.
cards.short_summary: A library-based setting for guided studying and academic coaching.
cards.evidence_claim: Le Moyne states that the first-floor Student Success Center has mentors and tutors available for individual and group sessions.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Falcone Library. Book tutoring when required and confirm current service hours before visiting.

cards.title: Bring the Draft to the Writing Center
cards.subtitle: First-floor help for papers and outlines
cards.notes: Bring a draft, assignment sheet, or outline and identify the passage or writing decision you want to discuss during the appointment.
cards.short_summary: A focused setting for developing papers with writing-tutor support.
cards.evidence_claim: Le Moyne locates the Writing Center on the library’s first floor next to the Student Success Center and QRC and offers writing appointments.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Falcone Library. Use the linked appointment system and verify current Writing Center availability.

cards.title: Settle Into a Lounge Chair
cards.subtitle: Casual upstairs Campus Center workspace
cards.notes: Choose a lounge chair for lower-intensity reading or laptop work, and expect recreational activity from the nearby pool and foosball tables.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge suited to casual work between classes rather than silence.
cards.evidence_claim: Le Moyne describes Corcoran Lounge as an upstairs space with lounge chairs and calls it a mix of fun and productivity.
cards.access_notes: Open to students under applicable Campus Center access rules; the pool and foosball tables make this a potentially active environment.

cards.title: Use the Den Without Ordering
cards.subtitle: Grewen Hall seating for study and meetings
cards.notes: Claim a table for laptop work or a small meeting, and choose this setting when normal dining activity will not disrupt your concentration.
cards.short_summary: A dining-area study option with seating explicitly available even without a purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: Le Moyne says The Den has seating for studying, group meetings, or late-night use even for people who are not purchasing food.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Grewen Hall. Seating can be used without buying food; consult current building and dining hours.

cards.title: Take the Reading Outside
cards.subtitle: Tables and chairs beside Reilly Hall
cards.notes: Bring a short reading or review task when the weather is comfortable; tables, chairs, and green space support an outdoor study session.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor terrace for reading or brief study between nearby classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Le Moyne describes Curtis Terrace beside Reilly Hall as having tables, chairs, and green space for reading or last-minute studying.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space beside Reilly Hall; practical access depends on weather and any current campus restrictions.
